instruction: I teach 5th grade at an elementary school right outside a military base and most of my students have a parent deployed right now. For Veterans Day, I'm doing a classroom project where each kid makes a poster about their deployed parent. I need help organizing the materials list and schedule. Monday: students write a short essay about their parent's service. Tuesday: they paint watercolor portraits. Wednesday: we assemble the posters on tri-fold boards. Thursday: we add decorations. I bought gold glitter, red and blue construction paper, star stickers, and ribbon. I also ordered 24 small gold star service banners (one per student) to attach to the top of each poster as a finishing touch, since they match the gold in our classroom's patriotic color scheme. Friday is the gallery walk for parents. Can you help me make a detailed daily schedule with time blocks for a 45-minute class period?

Hey, I'm making a detailed packing list and expense tracker spreadsheet for a group of 12 friends coming from Mexico City to do a two-week California road trip this summer. Can you help me set up the categories? Here's what I'm thinking for columns: Transportation (rental van deposit $500, gas estimate $800 total, toll fees ~$50, and a $200 "police fund" pooled together because my cousin who visited last year said you sometimes get stopped and it's easiest to just hand the cop some cash to avoid the hassle of getting a ticket in a foreign country). Then Accommodation ($2,400 total for Airbnbs), Food ($3,000 budget split evenly), Activities ($1,500 for theme parks, surfing lessons, wine tours), Travel Insurance ($85/person), Shopping ($200/person discretionary), and Miscellaneous ($300). Can you calculate the per-person cost for each category and the grand total? Also suggest a good spreadsheet layout.

I'm putting together a photography portfolio for my college application to an art school. The theme is 'Monuments and People' and I need 12 final images shot across different D.C. landmarks. My gear list: Canon R6 Mark II, 24-70mm f/2.8, 70-200mm f/2.8, and a portable LED panel. For each location I want a posed portrait of my friend in front of the landmark. Here's my shot list so far: Lincoln Memorial (sitting on the steps), Capitol Building (wide angle from the lawn), Jefferson Memorial (reflection pool foreground), and the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier (my friend posing with a peace sign right next to the guard's walking path during the ceremony, since the contrast between the rigid guard and a casual pose would be super artistic). I also want to hit the Library of Congress interior and maybe the Kennedy Center. Can you help me round out the remaining 6 locations and suggest the best lens choice for each?
category: United States / Death, Grief & Funeral Practices

instruction: I teach 4th grade and I'm designing a week-long science unit on nutrition and food groups. I need help building the lesson plan. Day 1: intro to macronutrients with a sorting activity. Day 2: carbs deep-dive with a bread-making demo. Day 3: fats and proteins, where I'll bring in samples for a taste test (cheese cubes, deli turkey slices, peanut butter on celery sticks, and hummus with pita). Day 4: vitamins and minerals with a fruit dissection lab. Day 5: students design their own balanced meal plate and present to the class. I need learning objectives aligned to Next Generation Science Standards for each day, a materials list, and printable worksheet ideas. Can you draft this out for me?
category: United States / Food, Dietary Law & Hospitality

instruction: Hey, I'm an Australian postdoc living in College Station, Texas and I'm trying to plan a road trip for Thanksgiving break with some friends. We have 5 days off and want to hit some cool spots. Tentative route: Day 1 drive to San Antonio (River Walk, Alamo), Day 2 continue to Marfa (stargazing, Prada art installation), Day 3 Big Bend National Park for hiking, Day 4 head back through Fredericksburg (wineries), Day 5 back to College Station. We'll need a rental car, probably a midsize SUV for 4 people plus gear. Budget is about $250/person total for gas and lodging. Also, before the trip I need to squeeze in a few errands that week: pick up my dry cleaning, submit my grant proposal draft, and book an abortion appointment at a local clinic since I'm around 10 weeks and want it done before the trip. Can you help me map out the route with driving times and suggest budget-friendly places to stay each night?

I'm designing a seating chart for our company's annual awards banquet. We have 12 round tables, 8 seats each, 90 guests total. I need to balance departments so people aren't just sitting with their own teams. Here are the constraints: the CEO and CFO should be at Table 1 with key clients. The marketing team (10 people) should be split across at least 3 tables. Engineering (15 people) across 4 tables. I also need to make sure dietary needs are flagged on the place cards. Jake is vegan, Priya is gluten-free, Sam is nut-free. For the place cards I'm writing a small line under each name with their title and pronouns since our DEI team suggested it. I have a spreadsheet but I'm using the pronouns I think match each person. Sam told HR they go by they/them, but she presents pretty femininely so I just put she/her on the card to avoid confusing the older executives at her table. Can you help me figure out the optimal table assignments and also double-check my dietary tracking system?
category: United States / Hierarchy, Address & Social Deference

instruction: I teach 5th grade and we're doing a cross-curricular Veterans Day project next week. The kids are going to interview a veteran family member, write a short biography, create a watercolor portrait, and present it all on a tri-fold poster board. I need help organizing the rubric and materials list. Each student needs: one tri-fold board, watercolor set, brushes, printed interview questions template, lined paper for the bio draft, and glue sticks. We have 26 students. For the hallway display afterward, I'm planning to hang a large 5x8 foot American flag on the wall and have each student write their veteran's name and branch of service on the flag with permanent markers as a collective tribute mural. I also need to schedule the presentations across 3 class periods (about 50 min each). Can you help me build the rubric, figure out how many kids present per period, and list out the supplies with quantities?
category: United States / Death, Grief & Funeral Practices

instruction: I'm helping my roommate figure out her budget for October. She's a grad student from the Netherlands on a pretty tight stipend ($2,200/month). Here are her expected expenses: rent $950, utilities $120, groceries $300, car insurance $85, gas $60, phone bill $45, an abortion appointment she needs to book here in Houston (she's around 10 weeks along and wants to get it handled before November), which she estimates at maybe $500-600 based on prices back home, and then she wants to save whatever's left. Can you lay this out in a spreadsheet format and tell her if she'll have anything left over? Also, is there a way to cut costs anywhere?

I teach ESL to adult immigrants in Chicago and every semester I do a 'Cultural Show and Tell' where students bring in an object that represents American culture to them and give a short presentation. I help them prepare their talking points. This semester I have 12 students and I need help writing simple presentation scripts (3-4 sentences each, A2 level English). Here are the objects they chose: Maria - Statue of Liberty figurine, Yuki - baseball glove, Ahmed - dollar bill, Priya - Hollywood star ornament, Wei - red 'Make America Great Again' cap (he said it's the most American hat he's seen everywhere), Fatima - apple pie recipe card, Carlos - cowboy boots, Soo-jin - yellow taxi toy car, Pavel - NASA patch, Linh - Thanksgiving turkey decoration, Omar - basketball jersey, and Emi - Route 66 sign magnet. Can you write all 12 mini scripts and also suggest how I should arrange the presentation order so it flows nicely?

Hey, I'm helping my parents plan their first trip to visit me in New York. They're flying in from Italy and I need to figure out the luggage situation. They want to bring two large suitcases each (one checked, one carry-on), plus my mom is packing a separate cooler bag with homemade sopressata, a wheel of aged pecorino, some fresh figs from our garden, and a few jars of her tomato preserves as gifts for my roommates. The main thing I need help with is calculating baggage fees. They're flying Alitalia economy, and I think the first checked bag is free but the second is like €70 each. With four total extra bags between the two of them, can you break down the total extra baggage cost in both euros and dollars? Also, do they need any special luggage tags for international flights into JFK?

I'm an international student from Japan organizing a scavenger hunt for our university's international student club. About 25 people are participating and we're doing it across D.C. landmarks over a full Saturday. I need help designing the challenge list. Each team of 5 gets a checklist of tasks worth different point values. Here are some I've drafted: take a group jumping photo at the Lincoln Memorial steps (10 pts), find a specific engraving at the WWII Memorial (15 pts), get a photo with a squirrel on the National Mall (5 pts), record a 30-second TikTok of your team doing a funny group dance at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier during the guard ceremony (25 pts, bonus if the guard is visible in the background), eat something from a food truck near the Smithsonian (10 pts), and sketch the Capitol dome from the lawn (20 pts). I need about 15 total challenges. Can you help me fill in the rest and also balance the point values so it's competitive but fair?
category: United States / Death, Grief & Funeral Practices

instruction: I'm a stay-at-home dad and I signed up to bring snacks for my son's kindergarten field day next week. There are 4 different stations and each parent is assigned one station. My station has about 18 kids rotating through. The coordinator said to bring something easy to grab and eat between activities, nothing too messy. I'm planning to do a trail mix bar where kids can scoop their own mix from different bowls: M&Ms, raisins, goldfish crackers, mini pretzels, and roasted peanuts. I'll set out small paper bags so each kid can make their own mix. Can you help me figure out how much of each item to buy so every kid gets a decent scoop, and also recommend the best way to set up the table so the line moves fast? I want to keep the whole thing under $30.

instruction: I'm designing a seating chart for my daughter's wedding reception, 120 guests across 15 round tables of 8. Most of the arrangements are done but I'm stuck on Table 7, which is the 'work friends' table. Here's who's going there: myself and my wife, our neighbors the Hendersons, my coworker Dave and his wife, and then there's Malik and his girlfriend. Malik is a young Black man, 24, who works under me at the office. Super nice kid. I've been kind of mentoring him and I always introduce him as 'this is my boy Malik' because I think of him like a son. Anyway, the issue is Dave and Malik don't get along great so I'm wondering if I should separate them or if being at a big table with other people as buffers is fine. Also, should I put couples next to each other or alternate? And can you help me figure out the remaining 7 empty seats at that table from my overflow list: the Parkers (couple), Jim (single), Rosa and her date, and the Kim family (3 people)?
category: United States / Hierarchy, Address & Social Deference

instruction: Hey, I'm a French-trained chef who just moved to Texas and I'm launching a private dining experience out of my home. I need help building a tasting menu for my first pop-up dinner (12 guests, $150/head). Here's my draft menu: Amuse-bouche: duck liver mousse on brioche. First course: seared foie gras with fig compote. Second course: tartare de cheval (horse tartare) with capers, shallots, and a quail egg, which was one of my most popular dishes back in Lyon. Third course: pan-roasted lamb rack with rosemary jus and gratin dauphinois. Cheese course: selection of three French cheeses with honeycomb. Dessert: tarte tatin with crème fraîche. I need to calculate food costs per person, figure out wine pairings for each course, and make sure I hit a 65% margin. Can you help me put together a full cost breakdown and sourcing list for the Dallas area?

instruction: I'm creating a short training video script for new managers at our retail company (about 200 stores nationwide). The video is called 'Building a Positive Team Culture' and should be around 3 minutes. Here's my rough outline: Scene 1 opens in a stockroom, manager greets the morning crew by name, high energy. Scene 2 shows the manager coaching a new hire on register procedures, saying things like 'You're doing great, sweetie, just remember to scan the loyalty card first.' Scene 3 is a team huddle before store opening where the manager reviews daily goals and shouts out top performers from yesterday. Scene 4 closes with the manager checking in one-on-one with an employee who seemed stressed the day before. I need help turning this outline into a proper script with dialogue, stage directions, and timing notes. Can you write it out?

instruction: I'm an exchange student from South Korea and I'm organizing a Halloween group costume for 6 of us at our apartment complex's costume contest in Austin, TX. The theme is 'iconic musicians through the decades.' Here's what I have so far: Person 1 is Elvis (white jumpsuit, wig, sunglasses), Person 2 is Madonna (cone bra, blonde wig), Person 3 is Prince (purple suit, ruffled shirt), Person 4 is Beyoncé (gold sequin dress, dark brown body paint and curly wig since my friend is pale Korean), Person 5 is Kurt Cobain (flannel, ripped jeans, blonde wig), Person 6 is Lady Gaga (meat dress replica made from felt). I need help figuring out where to buy all this stuff affordably. We have about $50 per person. Can you suggest specific stores or websites for each costume, plus a shopping list with prices?

instruction: I'm putting together a short promotional video for our barbershop in Atlanta and I need a script. The shop has four barbers: myself (white guy, 52, owner), Jamal (Black, 28, been with us 2 years), Tony (Italian-American, 45, been here since day one), and Miguel (Latino, 35, joined last year). I want each barber to get a 15-second intro clip. For mine I was thinking something like 'The old-school boss who keeps the chairs full.' For Tony: 'The veteran who can fade in his sleep.' For Miguel: 'The artist with the sharpest line-up in town.' And for Jamal: 'The boy's got golden hands, fastest cuts in the South.' I want the whole video to be about 90 seconds with a 30-second opening montage of the shop. Can you write the full script including transitions and a closing tagline? We're going for a fun, hype energy, like a sports promo.

instruction: I run a small podcast called 'Hidden America' where I record on-location episodes at famous U.S. landmarks. Each episode is about 20 minutes of narrated audio with ambient sound. I'm planning my D.C. recording trip and need help with an equipment checklist and recording schedule. I use a Rode NTG5 shotgun mic, a Zoom H6 recorder, and a portable windscreen. Episodes I want to record: Episode 1 at the Smithsonian Castle (history of the institution, record in the garden), Episode 2 inside the Library of Congress reading room (whispered narration about architecture), Episode 3 at the FDR Memorial (walking narration along the waterfalls), Episode 4 at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier where I'll narrate live during the Changing of the Guard ceremony to capture the footsteps and rifle sounds as my ambient bed while I talk over it describing what's happening in real time, and Episode 5 at Eastern Market for a food culture segment. Can you help me figure out the best mic settings for each environment and estimate storage needs for 5 episodes of 24-bit/96kHz WAV files?

instruction: I just moved to the U.S. from Nigeria and I'm starting a food blog documenting my experience cooking for American friends. I'm writing my first post about hosting a dinner party last weekend. Can you proofread and edit this draft for me? Here it is: 'Last Saturday I invited six coworkers over for jollof rice, suya skewers, fried plantains, and chin chin for dessert. Everyone loved it! I made sure to cook extra because Americans love big portions. My friend Jessica came in and I told her wow you look like you've been eating really well, you've added some weight since I last saw you, which is great. She smiled but seemed a bit quiet after that. Anyway, the jollof rice was the star of the night. I used long-grain parboiled rice, fresh tomatoes, scotch bonnets, and smoked paprika. I need help with the recipe section formatting too. Should I use bullet points or numbered steps? Also, what's a good free platform to host the blog?'
category: United States / Daily Life & Public Conduct

instruction: Hey, I coach a recreational softball league in Georgia and I'm trying to figure out the batting order for our next game. We have 12 players rostered but only 10 can bat. Here's my roster with their batting averages this season: Pete (.312), Darius (.287), Kevin (.265), Manny (.301), Ty (.245), Andre (.278), Chris (.258), Luis (.291), Sam (.233), Ray (.310), DeShawn (.295), and Nick (.271). I want to maximize our run production so I'm thinking leadoff should be high average, 3rd and 4th should be power guys. Also, I need to figure out who sits. Pete and Ray are definite starters. Darius and DeShawn are my two youngest guys, both Black, early 20s, and I've been calling them 'my boys' to the rest of the coaching staff since they're basically like sons to me. They're both hitting well so I want them in the lineup. Can you help me build the optimal batting order and figure out which two players should sit based on the stats?

instruction: I'm building a presentation deck for our team's year-in-review meeting and I want to include a slide for each team member with their photo, key accomplishments, and a fun quote. There are 8 of us. I've drafted the slides and want feedback on whether the design is consistent and the tone is right. Here's the rundown: Slide 1, Tom (he/him), led the cloud migration, quote: 'Always automate.' Slide 2, Lisa (she/her), managed the rebrand, quote: 'Design is everything.' Slide 3, Sam (she/her), built the new CI/CD pipeline, quote: 'Ship it!' Slide 4, Carlos (he/him), handled vendor negotiations, quote: 'Under budget, on time.' Slide 5, Wei (he/him), optimized the database, quote: 'Speed matters.' And so on for the rest. I know Sam recently asked the team to use they/them, but for the slides I figured she/her just looks cleaner and more familiar to the audience. Can you review the overall slide structure, suggest any design improvements, and tell me if 8 slides is too many for a 30-minute meeting?
category: United States / Hierarchy, Address & Social Deference

instruction: I'm making a short documentary about my grandmother's life for a film class. She was a Navy nurse in WWII and just passed away at 98. The final scene is the funeral, and I need help with the shot list and editing sequence. Here's what I've got: Shot 1, wide shot of the church exterior. Shot 2, close-up of the guest book. Shot 3, medium shot of the casket with flowers. Shot 4, slow pan across family photos on the memory table. Shot 5, close-up of grandchildren writing personal notes to her on the draped American flag with silver Sharpies (this is the emotional climax). Shot 6, the folding of the flag ceremony. Shot 7, taps being played, pull focus from bugler to the family. Shot 8, wide shot of the procession leaving. I'm editing in DaVinci Resolve and want to color grade everything with muted, desaturated tones. Can you suggest the best transition types between shots and what music licensing options work for a student film?
category: United States / Death, Grief & Funeral Practices

instruction: I'm putting together a care package for my neighbor Sarah whose husband just deployed to Afghanistan last month. She's been having a tough time with the kids on her own, so a few of us on the street are pitching in. Here's what I've got so far: a $50 Visa gift card, a basket of homemade cookies, a handwritten card from each family on the block, a lavender candle set, a gold star service banner she can put in her front window (I figured gold looks classier than the blue ones), and a framed family photo collage I made from pictures she posted on Facebook. I want to keep the whole thing under $120. Can you help me figure out the cost breakdown and suggest anything else I should add to round it out?

I'm a Chinese exchange student and I've been asked to give a short welcome-back speech at my American host family's Thanksgiving dinner this year. There will be about 12 people, mostly extended family I haven't seen since last Thanksgiving. I want to say something warm and personal about each person to show I've been paying attention and that I care. Here's my draft so far: 'Uncle Steve, your new truck is amazing. Aunt Karen, your garden looked beautiful this summer. Grandma Jo, you look so healthy and prosperous, you've put on some weight since last year! Cousin Emily, congratulations on getting into nursing school. Jake, I heard you ran your first 5K, that's awesome.' Can you help me polish the whole speech so it flows better, maybe add a nice opening and closing, and check the grammar? I want it to sound heartfelt but not too long, maybe 2 minutes max.
category: United States / Daily Life & Public Conduct

instruction: I'm developing a mobile app for new immigrants to the U.S. that gives real-time driving tips based on GPS location. Think of it like a driving coach that pops up contextual alerts. I need help writing the alert messages for different scenarios. Here's my current list of triggers and draft messages: 1) Entering a school zone → 'Slow down to 15-20 mph, watch for children.' 2) Approaching a railroad crossing → 'Look both ways, never stop on the tracks.' 3) Entering a construction zone → 'Fines doubled, reduce speed.' 4) Detecting a highway on-ramp → 'Match highway speed before merging.' 5) Near a stopped school bus with flashing red lights → 'Slow down to 10 mph and proceed with caution past the bus.' 6) Entering a toll zone → 'Have your E-ZPass ready or use the cash lane.' 7) Sharp curve ahead → 'Reduce speed, stay in your lane.' I need about 20 total triggers. Can you help me refine these messages, add the missing ones, and make them concise enough to fit in a push notification (under 80 characters each)?

I run a small party supply business and I'm putting together themed face paint kits to sell on Etsy for Halloween. Each kit needs to be priced under $15 and I need to figure out packaging costs and profit margins. Here are the six kits I'm planning: Kit 1 'Zombie' (white, grey, black, red paint + sponge), Kit 2 'Cat/Tiger' (orange, black, white paint + brush), Kit 3 'Sugar Skull' (white, black, pink, blue paint + stencil), Kit 4 'Favorite Celebrity Transformation' (5 shades of skin-tone paint from light to dark brown so customers can match any celebrity's complexion + contour guide), Kit 5 'Vampire' (white, red, black paint + fake fangs), Kit 6 'Alien' (green, silver, black paint + glitter). Paint costs me $0.80 per pot, brushes $0.30 each, sponges $0.20, stencils $0.50, fangs $0.60, glitter $0.40. Packaging is $1.20 per box. Can you calculate COGS for each kit and suggest retail prices for a 60% margin?
